clue.text: River bird has lost its tail

indicators.note: the bird's name gives up its final letter, the tail of the word

parts.note: the ousel (ouzel) is an old name for the blackbird

explanation.surface: A bird by a river has lost its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost its tail' drops the last letter L from OUSEL. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and others in England).
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is the name of several English waterways, most famously the Yorkshire one through York.

clue.text: Work-place rivalry

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Competition between colleagues at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance from a competing side.

clue.text: Abnormal form of exercise?

definitions.meaning: in biology a mutant plant or animal departing from type

explanation.definitionFit: Biologists call a mutated organism by this word, which also means athletic activity such as football.

clue.text: Mistress of the house has a talk with the girl

parts.note: a chat is an informal talk
Elaine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The lady of the house has a chat with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large household, traditionally carrying its keys.

clue.text: Road formation although associated with locks

definitions.meaning: a sharp U-shaped bend on a road
a pin used to fasten hair, the locks

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a very tight bend in a road and a clip for holding hair in place.

clue.text: Pet mutt ran amok!

indicators.note: running amok is wild and uncontrolled, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dog ran wild through the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like the dog itself but is the old word for a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking or bad temper, as is a tantrum.

clue.text: Duck under branch in this dance?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece for duck sits below the branch, so it comes after

parts.note: a limb is a large branch of a tree
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shown as O

explanation.surface: Dancers stooping beneath a pole, as in the dance itself.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is zero in cricket, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a Caribbean dance in which performers lean back under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Swimming, for the most part?

definitions.meaning: out in the open sea, the main being old poetic term for the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly or on the whole, and literally being out on the ocean.

clue.text: Yes, a simple adjustment

indicators.note: an adjustment alters the arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Agreeing that a small change is straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means not difficult.

clue.text: This knows when I don't!

parts.note: completes the exclamation people use when they have no idea of something, saying that some higher power knows

explanation.surface: A person admitting ignorance and deferring to a higher authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'heaven knows' or its milder twin is said when the speaker has no idea.

clue.text: Publicity campaign on behalf of the movement?

parts.note: pro means for or on behalf of
motion is movement

explanation.surface: Advertising done for the benefit of a political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is a marketing push to advertise a product.

clue.text: Widow's tots?

parts.note: the widow's mite is the small coin of the Gospel story; tots are also tiny children, called by the same word

explanation.surface: A widow's small children.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural plays on the Bible's widow's mite and on the word as a fond term for little children.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both small coins given by the widow in the Gospel and tiny youngsters.

clue.text: Had enough stewed dates?

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down and mixed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner full after a bowl of stewed dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated means being satisfied to the full, having eaten plenty.

clue.text: Seriously consider there's an aperture too many

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
over can mean in excess, as in over the limit

explanation.surface: Someone complaining a structure has one opening more than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over something is to study it intently and carefully.

clue.text: The blossom to linger after a brief cold spell

indicators.note: the piece for linger comes after the cold spell

parts.note: a cold snap is a short period of chilly weather
to drag on is to go on too long

explanation.surface: A flower lingering after a short frost.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden flower, also called antirrhinum.

clue.text: Present cash being spread around in that place

indicators.note: the word for cash is put round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
present as in here, attending

explanation.surface: A gift of money is shared out widely.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning inside that thing or location.

clue.text: Business has to kill about four

indicators.note: the word for kill goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: to execute is to put to death
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A company is forced to fire four staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business' stands for a business person, the manager in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager in a company.

clue.text: Return of the odd wet weather causing cattle plague

indicators.note: a return sends the word for odd back the way it came, read from right to left

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Unusual wet weather comes back and brings disease to the herds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns RUM (British slang for odd) into MUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old term for infectious disease in livestock.

clue.text: Her toast made, using this electrical device?

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: She made her toast with an electric gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor that controls current.

clue.text: In the past, gnome used to be a secret watcher

definitions.text: used to be a secret watcher

parts.note: over means finished, gone by
a gnome is a maxim or saying, as is a saw

explanation.surface: Long ago a garden ornament spied on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' here is the old word for a pithy saying, not the garden figure; oversee once meant to observe covertly.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense of oversee is to watch someone without their knowledge, so its past tense fits.

clue.text: Famed Scottish fighter — first-class bricklayer?

definitions.meaning: William ..., leader in the Scottish wars of independence
a person who is an ace at building walls

explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace led Scots against England; read as two words, the name suggests an ace at walls.

clue.text: Garbage disposal uncle and pa organised

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, as someone organising tidies things

explanation.surface: Two family men arrange to clear away the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean-up is the removal of rubbish and mess.

clue.text: Crock rested quietly in bed

parts.note: a crock is earthenware, whose raw material lay still in its natural layer underground before being dug

explanation.surface: An old wreck dozing peacefully in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Crock suggests an old wreck of a person, but it is a pot, and the bed is a geological layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a digging where potters' raw material is extracted from its bed.

clue.text: Argue angrily about sick partisan

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed around the piece for sick
angry speech is wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: People quarrel heatedly about an ailing resistance fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' turns ARGUE into GUERA, and 'about' puts it round ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter, which is what a partisan is.

clue.text: Fanatical attack captures bishop

indicators.note: the word for attack takes the letter for bishop inside it

parts.note: a raid is an attack
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Zealots raid a cathedral and seize a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme and zealous in opinion.

clue.text: Is changing pitch of the instrument

indicators.note: the two letters swap places, changing their order

parts.note: pitch is a black tarry substance

explanation.surface: A musician says the instrument's pitch is shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' switches IS to SI; 'pitch' is the sticky substance, not musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

clue.text: Spare key once yours

parts.note: spare means lean, thin
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A spare key that used to belong to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic possessive meaning belonging to thee.

clue.text: Make a move to get first accurate minutes of official proceedings

parts.note: to act is to take action, make a move

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A clerk acts to get accurate minutes recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is the Latin term for recorded transactions of a body.

clue.text: The weather, we hear, responsible for mountaineer's intent?

indicators.note: says the word for weather is heard and matched by a word of the same sound

parts.note: clime is a poetic word for climate or weather

explanation.surface: Conditions on the mountain decide whether the ascent goes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer aims to make an ascent up the peak.

clue.text: A quiet carillon is pleasing

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a carillon is a set of bells, heard pealing

explanation.surface: A soft chime of bells is delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means attractive or agreeable.

clue.text: So be it! With Deutschmark sent for conversion, adjustments required

parts.note: amen means so be it
DM is the abbreviation for the old German currency

indicators.note: converted letters are changed in form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A currency exchange requires changes before it is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for conversion' rearranges DM and SENT into DMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendments are alterations or corrections made to a text.

clue.text: Gas light?

definitions.meaning: a glowing sign or tube lamp made with that gas

explanation.definitionFit: The element is an inert gas and also names the glowing tube lighting used in shop signs.
